text:
The son most likely prevails as an intended third-party beneficiary, since the contract directed payment to him and the landscaper meant it as a gift. His rights hadn't vested when the owner and landscaper changed the payee. But the landscaper had already fully performed, and under Restatement (Second) §311 and the modern majority view, a modification after performance can't cut off a donee beneficiary's rights. The contract was a promise to pay a third party, not an assignment, so B fits better than A.

CONFIDENCE: 70
